text:
sara_sales: Hey team — kickoff for Trident POC this afternoon. Customer wants Private deployment behind their VPC. Quick asks: do we have a minimal firewall allowlist, egress IP behavior, and a ballpark of incremental network costs for PrivateLink vs peering? Need to reply to their netops by EOD.
ali_netops: TL;DR checklist + guidance below. PrivateLink recommended when customer wants isolated control plane + simplified auditing. Peering ok for low-latency intra-account traffic but harder for cross-tenant isolation.
ali_netops: Minimal outbound allowlist we typically ask for (customer side to permit outbound to Redwood endpoints):
```
- TCP 443 to: REDWOOD_PRIVATELINK_ENDPOINT_IPS (we'll provide the /32 list)
- NTP / UDP 123 (if they want time sync from our agents) - optional
- DNS (53 UDP/TCP) to resolver if they use custom DNS for endpoint resolution
```
matt_se: Important: if they plan TLS-inspect on egress, SNI rewriting breaks model request routing. Recommend a no-TLS-inspect exception for hostnames under our certs.
julie_security: +1 on the TLS-inspect note. Also need attestation on key rotation windows and KMS integration details for Private deployments. We'll send the security questionnaire section later.
ali_netops: Egress IP behavior: with PrivateLink we present a fixed set of endpoint IPs (customer sees those as service IPs). With peering, source IP preservation depends on NAT placement. If they require client srcIP preservation to downstream services, peering with 1:1 NAT at their edge is simpler.
ali_netops: Cost tradeoffs (very rough):
- PrivateLink: you pay endpoint-hour + data processing egress per GB (customer-facing cloud costs vary by region). Simpler operational model.
- Peering: no endpoint-hour but could increase NAT/EIP costs on the customer's side and more routing ops for cross-account. Could also complicate multi-AZ failover.
sara_sales: Do we have a sample firewall snippet I can drop into their ticket? Prefer short so netops can paste.
ali_netops: Use this minimal copy/paste (replace ips/placeholders):
```
# Allow Redwood PrivateLink endpoints
- proto: tcp
  ports: 443
  dest: 203.0.113.10/32 # redwood-privatelink-1 (example)
- proto: tcp
  ports: 443
  dest: 203.0.113.11/32 # redwood-privatelink-2
# DNS to your resolver if using private DNS (optional)
- proto: udp
  ports: 53
  dest: 10.0.0.2/32
```
matt_se: Also ask them to confirm whether they will route model telemetry/metrics over the same path — if not, we can recommend splitting telemetry to a separate egress path to avoid peering costs.
julie_security: For the security Q: we'll need their SOC2 conformance doc and whether they're OK with an SOC2 addendum. I'll DM the questionnaire link to @sara_sales.
deploy-bot: ticket created: ENG-NET-4021 — "Trident POC: private deploy network handoff" assigned to ali_netops. Due: 2025-06-18.
sara_sales: Thanks — I'll send the firewall snippet + note about TLS inspect and ask for their preferred pattern (PrivateLink vs peering). I'll loop in legal if they ask about SOC2. Can we get that /32 list and cost bullets by 3pm?
ali_netops: I'll publish the endpoint IP list to the ticket and add a brief cost bullet list by 2:30pm.
matt_se: Happy to join the call at 4pm if needed to clarify SNI/TLS issues.
julie_security: I'll prepare the security checklist and add a note about KMS integration options.
sara_sales: Great — closing the loop here. Will update customer and post any follow-ups in this thread. :thumbsup:
